sections.learningObjectives:
- Describe the stages of the revenue cycle from patient access through follow-up.
- Explain the medical office assistant's role in supporting revenue cycle activities within scope.
- Recognize the importance of financial accuracy in coding, billing, and payment posting.
- Identify common claim issues such as rejections, denials, and errors and the correct escalation steps.
- Apply basic coverage and patient-responsibility concepts to everyday front- and back-office tasks.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of the revenue cycle as a relay race: each teammate (registration, coding, billing, payment) must pass the baton correctly or the race, and the payment, does not finish.

### Question 2

Before you can bake a cake you need the recipe and ingredients. Patient access is gathering the recipe and ingredients so the rest of the process works.

### Question 3

Imagine mailing a letter with the wrong address or zip code: it bounces back. A wrong name or ID on a claim makes it bounce back the same way.

### Question 4

Charge capture is like a cashier scanning every item at checkout; if an item is not scanned, the store does not get paid for it.

### Question 5

A coder is like a translator who turns the doctor's notes into a special code language; the MOA helps by making sure the notes are complete and in the right place.

### Question 6

A claim is like the invoice you send after mowing a lawn; it lists what you did and how much to pay.

### Question 7

The MOA is like the person at the front desk of a race who makes sure every runner has the right number pinned on before they start.

### Question 8

A clean claim is like turning in homework that is complete and neat so the teacher can grade it without asking questions.

### Question 9

A copay is like a small fixed ticket price you pay each time you go, while the rest is covered by the plan.

### Question 10

A deductible is like the first few dollars you pay yourself before a friend starts helping split the cost.

### Question 11

Coinsurance is like splitting the bill with a friend by percentage: you pay 20 percent and they pay 80 percent.

### Question 12

A prior authorization is like asking permission before a big purchase so you know it will be paid for.

### Question 13

Checking eligibility early is like checking you have enough money before you go shopping, so there are no surprises at the register.

### Question 14

A superbill is like a store receipt that lists everything purchased, so the billing team knows what to charge for.

### Question 15

You would not charge for a cake you never baked; the notes are proof the service really happened, so the bill must match the proof.

### Question 16

A remittance advice is like the note a store leaves in a returned package explaining why part of your money is coming back.

### Question 17

A/R is like money friends owe you after you paid for pizza; it is yours, but you have not received it yet.

### Question 18

Imagine a restaurant bill with an extra entree you never ordered; you would want it fixed. Patients deserve correct bills too.

### Question 19

If you are not sure which key opens a lock, you ask the person who knows instead of forcing the wrong key.

### Question 20

A patient statement is like the final bill you get after your share of a shared meal is calculated.

### Question 21

A clearinghouse is like a post office that checks the address and stamps before forwarding your letter.

### Question 22

The payer is like the friend who agreed to cover most of the dinner bill while you cover a small part.

### Question 23

A charge is like the price tag put on each item in a store before the customer pays.

### Question 24

Coding is like turning a recipe into a shopping list of codes, and billing is like sending that list to be paid.

### Question 25

It is like building a sandwich: bread (registration), filling (charges and codes), and top slice (billing and payment), with cleanup (follow-up) at the end.

### Question 26

If your bus pass expired, you would get a new one before riding; updating insurance works the same way.

### Question 27

Collecting the copay at the door is like paying for your movie ticket before you watch, instead of the theater chasing you later.

### Question 28

If the cashier forgets to scan one item in your cart, the store does not get paid for it. Same idea.

### Question 29

If you wait weeks to send an invoice, you get paid weeks later. Missing the invoice means never getting paid.

### Question 30

Diagnosis codes are like labeling the problem (why), while procedure codes label the fix (what was done).

### Question 31

CPT codes are like naming each tool the mechanic used and each repair performed, so the bill lists the work done.

### Question 32

If CPT codes name the repairs, HCPCS codes name the parts and special equipment used.

### Question 33

Medical necessity is like needing a cast for a broken arm; it must match the problem and be backed up by the notes.

### Question 34

Claim scrubbing is like proofreading an essay before turning it in so the teacher does not hand it back for mistakes.

### Question 35

A rejection is like the post office returning your letter unread; a denial is like the recipient reading it and saying no.

### Question 36

If you write the wrong apartment number on a package, it gets returned; the mistake is in the address, not the contents.

### Question 37

An ERA is like getting your bank statement online instead of by mail; the information is the same, just digital.

### Question 38

If you record a deposit in the wrong column of your piggy bank ledger, you will think you have more or less money than you really do.

### Question 39

An aging report is like sorting your IOUs by how long ago each friend borrowed money, so you know who to remind first.

### Question 40

An appeal is like politely asking a teacher to re-check a test answer you believe was graded wrong, with your work shown as proof.

### Question 41

A timely filing deadline is like a coupon that expires; use it before the date or it is no good.

### Question 42

If the teacher marks an answer wrong because of a typo, you fix the typo and resubmit, not erase the whole test.

### Question 43

If a store agrees to sell you a $100 item for $80, the $20 difference is like a contractual adjustment.

### Question 44

A contractual adjustment is a planned discount you agreed to; bad debt is money you lent and never got back.

### Question 45

You wait until the group meal bill is split before asking each friend for their share, not before.

### Question 46

You would not promise your friend you can get them into a movie for free without checking the tickets first.

### Question 47

Upcoding is like claiming you did ten hours of work when you only did five; it inflates the bill unfairly.

### Question 48

Downcoding is like doing ten hours of work but only billing for five; the work was done but not fairly reported.

### Question 49

Unbundling is like charging separately for the bun, patty, and cheese instead of one price for a burger.

### Question 50

Fraud is cheating on purpose, abuse is bending the rules, and an error is an accidental typo; all matter but they are different.

### Question 51

If a teammate asks you to cheat on a test, the right move is to say no and tell the teacher, not to cheat.

### Question 52

The MOA is like the person who makes sure the order slip is filled out completely before handing it to the chef.

### Question 53

If the ticket booth says your pass does not cover this ride, you tell the group so you can decide together what to do.

### Question 54

The NPI is like a driver's license number for a provider, so everyone knows exactly who is billing.

### Question 55

The CMS-1500 is the special paper (or electronic version) a doctor's office uses to ask for payment.

### Question 56

Sending a claim electronically is like emailing instead of mailing a letter; it arrives instantly and with fewer lost envelopes.

### Question 57

A complete claim is like a complete mailing address plus a list of everything in the package, so it reaches the right place and can be processed.

### Question 58

If you put money in the wrong piggy bank, you move it to the right one and tell an adult, not pretend it never happened.

### Question 59

If your order is returned with a note saying why, you read the note and ask the manager how to fix it, not ignore it.

### Question 60

A correct list of who owes you money tells you who to remind and how much, so you collect the right amount.

### Question 61

You can tell a friend about how much a meal might cost by checking the menu, but you would not promise the exact total with tax and tip.

### Question 62

The mistake happened when the birthday was first typed, like writing the wrong birthday on a party invitation.

### Question 63

Getting paid at the time of service is like getting paid when you finish the job instead of chasing the money later.

### Question 64

A financial policy is like house rules for a game, so everyone knows the rules before playing.

### Question 65

You would not erase a friend's debt without checking the rules and the person in charge.

### Question 66

If water keeps leaking because the faucet is left on, you turn off the faucet, not mop forever.

### Question 67

If you have $300 and earn $10 a day, it would take 30 days to collect it all; days in A/R works the same way.

### Question 68

If the agreed price is $150 and you pay 20 cents of every dollar, you pay $30; the plan pays the other $120.

### Question 69

If you need to save $1,000 and already have $350, you still need $650 more.

### Question 70

Twenty percent of one dollar is twenty cents, so twenty percent of $100 is $20.

### Question 71

If you miss a contest deadline, you check whether they accept late entries before giving up.

### Question 72

If the receipt does not match what was actually bought, that is a warning sign someone should look into.

### Question 73

If someone changes the numbers on purpose to get more money, that is cheating, not an accident.

### Question 74

If you wait two weeks to send every invoice, your money arrives two weeks later, and some invoices get lost.

### Question 75

You pay the bill that is due tomorrow before the one that is due next month.

### Question 76

You check whether you already sent the invitation before sending it twice to the same person.

### Question 77

A front-end denial is like being turned away at the door; a back-end denial is like getting rejected after your application was reviewed.

### Question 78

If a problem needs an expert, you hand it to the expert instead of guessing.

### Question 79

If most of the money people owe you has been owed for a long time, it means you have not been collecting.

### Question 80

If the cash register says $100 but you only count $90, you find the missing $10 before closing up.

### Question 81

Charging only for what really happened means you get paid fairly and you never overcharge.

### Question 82

Surprise billing is like being charged extra after a meal because part of the kitchen was out of your plan's network and you did not know.

### Question 83

If the library has two cards for the same person, books get checked out to the wrong card; a clean patient index prevents the same mix-up with bills.
